title: feat(seat): orchestrator_tick.py — the heartbeat's dispatch list
body:
Why this change, and what it measures.

The round-9 throughput pre-study's stall ledger (§5 of PRESTUDY-throughput.md) attributes today's dominant losses to information stalls, not gate walls: buffered logs, misread states, stale queue entries, and a 9.5 h window where the information existed (six ci-watch alerts, a 10-entry verdicted queue) and nobody consumed it. This PR lands the anti-stall deliverable: `tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py`, one read-only command the heartbeat runs every few minutes. It prints a DISPATCH LIST — everything needing a decision or a seat — measured from the live sources at tick time (GitHub API for PR/CI/mergeability, the tree for rows/carries/pins, the log file for train state), never from memory, and never from the queue file's stale fields alone (each queued PR's state and head is re-read from the API and diffed against the queue's claim). It does NOT act: no pushes, no merges, no closes. A section whose read fails prints UNREADABLE — a silent skip is the stall class it exists to kill. The first line of every board is provenance ("BOARD measured from origin/main at <sha>, <UTC>"): a stale board self-identifies.

## Head

`268858e5478b2c4852655c96144118224556c6a2` is the orchestrator's recarry of main into the previous head. It is not a clean merge of the live head and main (parent 1 ffc68d35 is not the live pull-request head 268858e5), so prepr checked this head.

`268858e5478b2c4852655c96144118224556c6a2` merges main `cb7cb25` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

ffc68d354543f5eac993fc58ac7a05e59c2ae95e (the ETA-DEVIATION section; everything below measured at 137a78fe9/be578c9bd49 lineage and re-taken here where figures changed). Figures at this head: self-test 83 checks, 0 failed; layout GUARD 0 refusals. New: the ETA section — three deviation sources by precision: (1) the train beat's age vs 2x the 480s watcher heartbeat while the train python is alive (the wedged-or-dead detector that would have flagged today's 4h wedge at minute 16); (2) required lanes pending past 2x tests/ci_budgets.json's recorded critical_path_minutes (the one measured baseline; per-lane medians are not invented); (3) the orchestrator's optional ETAS file beside the queue (pr=<n> expected-by=<ISO> note=<text>), absent file, no findings. Self-test: one firing + one all-clear per source. (watcher-seat operating-mode docs plus the main-red dispatch briefs; the soundness fixes landed at bd49c8159, earlier evidence at be578c9bb, re-taken here where figures changed). Figures at this head: self-test 77 checks, 0 failed; layout GUARD 0 refusals; the provenance line asserted to print on the empty board. New since bd49c8159: the tick's watcher-seat operating mode and the orchestrator operating contract are documented in the docstring and INSTRUMENTS.md; every failed lane at main's tip — required or not — becomes a fixer dispatch brief (context, job id + error line from the check-run output, suspected class, dispatch instruction; ci-autofix bot lanes lead with the ci-autofix rule and quote the job's summary line), one output read per red lane capped at five; self-test arms cover the required-lane brief (four fields) and the bot-lane brief (autofix rule first). A main-side issue the orchestrator cannot resolve in one short turn is fixer work; the orchestrator's duty is routing, not diagnosing. (the watcher-seat operating-mode docs; the soundness fixes below landed at bd49c8159, earlier evidence measured at be578c9bb and re-taken where the figure changed). Figures re-taken at this head: self-test 75 checks, 0 failed; layout GUARD 0 refusals; the provenance line now asserted to print on the empty board (null-control arm). The docs delta only: the tick's INSTRUMENTS.md entry and docstring now name the watcher-seat operating mode (run by a watcher seat on a ~4-minute loop — cron firings skip while a turn runs; notify only on actionable events; never diagnose or fix) and the orchestrator operating contract it assumes (short turns; over-a-minute scripts run background; findings are dispatched, not merely printed).

## Design

Seven sections (TRAIN, PRS, WORKERS, PLAN, MAIN, STATE, REPLAN), one line per fact, `-> ` on a finding, `--json` for machine use, `--only` to limit sections; `--queue` may repeat.

- TRAIN: train liveness (pgrep; two live trains = a merge race; a nonempty queue with no train = a dead train), queue entries vs merged-into-main (prune), log tail and sibling .rc, prepr slots (cap 4).
- PRS, per open PR: latest check-run per name (lowercase conclusions, latest-run-wins; pending is not a pass) as GREEN/RUN/RED; `cancelled`/`startup_failure`/`timed_out` named separately as rerun items (they block invisibly); reds unanswered in ## Red checks; missing delivery row in the three-dot diff; queue verdict with the head moved past it and no carry; DIRTY/BLOCKED; ZERO-run heads (approve_held_runs, not a fixer); required contexts ABSENT at a head; twin open PRs at one head; claim-file touches whose `# claims-for:` is not VERSION; behind-main past --behind-max; body staleness (head moved past the body's last edit; heads <1h old skipped; one batched GraphQL read); stale tvofi owner review on code-owned PRs (CODEOWNERS last-match rule) and owner-review mandate-cite vs the in-force mandate id.
- WORKERS: seats judged from the work dispatched for them — head moved (DONE?), unchanged with no new CI completion after --grace-hours 0.5h (a PR gate runs 40-55m) → STALLED?; no PR yet OK inside --stall-hours.
- PLAN: roster through roster_lib (the one schema reader): newly unblocked groups (start a fixer), blocked groups name the blocker, deferred stays deferred.
- MAIN: main's tip; the ruleset's required contexts re-read every tick (never a remembered list); non-required nightly/record-class reds; the mandate through budget_raise_gate's own mandate_state (imported, never copied) with an expiry warning under 2h remaining; action-pin drift (one shared action at two refs); checkout staleness; API-quota headroom (warn under 20% of the hour); policy-corpus drift (newest commit touching the policy paths vs a one-line state file beside the queue — the tick's only write, outside the repo).
- STATE (read-only; the write stays in the per-merge beat): handover `updated-for:` vs origin/main's tip, merged PRs with no delivery row, merges with no #201 comment carrying the sha (cap 10 search calls), declared-Closes vs actually-closed per PR merged in 24h (cap 10, 2 calls each) — each nonzero names `state_docs.py --push` or the owed record beat.
- REPLAN (detection only; the item names the owed action): QUEUED-STALE (pinned verdict vs live head), prune-merged entries, repeated TRAIN STOPPED at one pr+step (pull the entry, dispatch a fixer), roster groups whose brief paths intersect an open PR's files (file fetches capped to queued PRs), done resumes whose commit is not in main, owner-gated groups with the oldest issue's age, the throughput stall (verdicted green entry + no train + main idle >20m → "fire the train"), undispositioned open issues (cap 15 oldest; a row, a roster group, or the plan's Delivery-status region counts — prose does not), handoff orphans (bus.sh orphans run as a subprocess, output parsed).

Owner input considered (each input → where it landed):

| input | where it landed |
|---|---|
| 1. heartbeat strategy as specified | TRAIN (train/queue/log), PRS (reds → fixers), PLAN (newly unblocked), WORKERS (liveness/DONE?/STALLED?), MAIN (red main admits nothing); the acting half stays the orchestrator's |
| 2. read-back, not memory | every section reads at tick time; queue verdicts verified against the live API head; UNREADABLE on any failed read (self-tested) |
| 3. more mechanical items | required-absent, twin heads, claim stamps, mandate freshness + expiry, pin drift, nightly-class main reds, main divergence, race/dead train, rate headroom, policy drift |
| 4. nudge.md as prior art | ported mechanical: steps 3, 4, 8, 11/15, 16, 17 and the reportable half of 12. Left behind as judgement (not tree/API-reportable): verdict-bus watching, reviewer-owed dispatch, 15-minute worktree-recency, post-merge duties, stamps, hold overlays |
| 5. token cost | see Figures — estimated ~6-12k tokens per manual tick vs ~2-3k per instrument tick; breakeven 1-2 ticks; acting turns NOT saved |

Alternatives considered, for the reviewer to check against: (a) extending ci-watch.sh — alerts on NEW states only, holds no queue/roster/worker model, and a signature file is the opposite of read-back-every-tick; (b) queue_pre_flight.py — admission-time validation, not a whole-board heartbeat; complementary; (c) a shell sweep — needs JSON parsing, ISO time arithmetic, roster wave logic and the gate's mandate grammar; shell re-implements all four; (d) not building — the stall ledger's dominant row is exactly unconsumed information.

## Mutation proof

Inverting the claims-stamp comparison in the reviewed head e31862881: `python3 tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py --self-test` → `39 checks, 3 failed`, exit 1; restored → 0 failed. At the current head the self-test is 66 checks; a mutation of any single detect arm reddens its all-clear twin (the arms are built as firing/all-clear pairs).

## Null control

The self-test's null control: an all-clear board (one green PR with its row, all groups done, live mandate, matching pins, no issues) runs all seven sections and prints the provenance line plus `DISPATCH LIST: empty (nothing needs a decision)`, zero findings. Live subset at the current head: `--only TRAIN,MAIN` against the real board printed 0 findings.

## Figures

- `python3 tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py --self-test` → `orchestrator_tick self-test: 83 checks, 0 failed` (exit 0), re-taken at ffc68d354543f5eac993fc58ac7a05e59c2ae95e; the arms run sections in production order via run() itself, stub gh method-sensitively, assert the provenance line on the empty board, and pin both main-red brief shapes.
- `python3 tests/layout.py` at bd49c8159 → `layout: GUARD: 0 refusal(s) against 4878463cb182`; the head's checks: 23 pass, 1 pending, 15 skipping, none red.
- Live board at bd49c8159 (re-measured at 137a78fe9 for the brief reads: +1 call per red lane, capped at five): full tick → 91 API calls at 21 open PRs, 75 findings; `--only TRAIN,MAIN` → 6 calls, 0 findings. (`--json`'s `api_calls`; measured.)
- Token cost (ESTIMATES, assumptions stated): a manual tick re-derives the sweep from conversation memory — ASSUMING ~15-25 tool outputs of 200-600 tokens plus ~0.5-1k of reconstruction prose → ~6-12k tokens/tick, ~240-480k over ~40+ ticks (the brief's figure). The instrument's list ≈ 75-100 lines ≈ ~2-3k tokens/tick → ~80-120k over 40 ticks. Breakeven: 1-2 ticks. NOT saved: acting turns (dispatches, folds, merges). The instrument SPENDS ~91 API calls per full tick at 21 open PRs (measured; quota, not tokens) — per-item caps: unrecorded merges 10, closes 10 (2 calls each, oldest first), owner reviews 10, issue dispositions 15, contested-file fetches queued-PRs-only.
- STALL_AFTER = 20 min provenance: the throughput pre-study's shortest measured stop today was the ~1 h 20 m read-back dead air (13:50→15:10Z) and the longest a 9.5 h absence window; a green head's own CI runs 40-55 m, so 20 m of idle main with a verdicted green entry already means a decision is overdue. It fired live at bd49c8159 (#2143 verdicted and green, main idle 67 m).

## Red checks

- Soundness review, three defects proven at be578c9bb, fixed at bd49c8159: (1) orphans() parsed bus.sh's usage stderr as refs — the subcommand lives in unmerged #2112; now a non-zero exit is ONE finding, never data (self-test: usage lines produce no ref flags). (2) The unrecorded-merge search used gh's `-f` POST form, which 404s — now `--method GET`, and the self-test's stub 404s any search call not carrying the method, so the arm fails loudly on the POST form. (3) The mandate-cite check read the live mandate id that only the MAIN section sets, while PRS runs first — the read is now hoisted before PRS, and a production-order self-test runs run() itself and asserts the drift fires. All three verified on the live board at bd49c8159: one unavailable line for orphans, a live record-beat finding naming 8 unrecorded merges via GET, and three real PRs (#2063, #2112, #2115) flagged for citing the expired mandate 6067089637.
- `layout` + `fast (3.14)` at e31862881 (`layout: GUARD: 2 refusal(s)`, and pr-contract's downstream red): the file cited the retired path .claude/workflows/budget_raise_gate.py twice as a `_module` fallback candidate (the gate moved to tools/policy/ in 3b0a39216). Fix: both candidates dropped, the tools/policy/ path kept (a667ef090); the guard now prints `0 refusal(s)`. The cheaper detector is tests/layout.py itself — it ran in CI; the process gap was that this seat did not run it on the branch diff before the first push; it has run before every push since.
- `pr-contract` at e31862881 and at a667ef090 (the body did not answer the then-open reds): answered here; the body was re-taken whole at each head rather than patched (three-round rule).

## Forward-carry

none — this PR is the instrument the throughput pre-study's stall ledger (§5) and §4.2 item 4 named; the sibling pre-flight (P5/queue_pre_flight) belongs to its own seat and is not owed here.

## Friction

none
